title: Scalar compatibility of the normalized projective-line splitting and trace
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. For a standing base $S$, put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ and $q:P\to S$. Let $L_R=R_P(1)[2]$ and let $s_R:R_S(1)[2]\oplus R_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{*,R}L_R$ be the splitting with components the twisted shifted unit and the scalar-extended Kummer class $h_R$ of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Set $t_R=\operatorname{pr}_2s_R^{-1}$ [def-amb-p1-trace]. Use the canonical balanced isomorphisms $T_T(R_T(1))\simeq B_T(1)$, sending $(z\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $z\otimes\varphi(a)b$, and their shifted and direct-sum versions. Let $\beta_q:T_SRq_{*,A}\to Rq_{*,B}T_P$ be the proper counit-transpose map [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Then, under these identifications,
$$\beta_q(L_A)\,T_S(s_A)=s_B,\qquad t_B\,\beta_q(L_A)=T_S(t_A).$$
These equations are equations of the specified derived morphisms and impose no flatness hypothesis on $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Charts: Kummer classes come from Z/ell^n, and the splitting into two free rank-one summands; retained Steps 5 and 6

proof.text: Normalize the scalar identifications before comparing arrows. For T=S,P, the sheaves A_T and A_T(1) are flat, and A_T(1) is locally free of rank one by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Their degree-zero complexes and shifts are K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. Thus [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes their scalar extension by ordinary tensor. The balanced map (z\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto z\otimes\varphi(a)b has inverse z\otimes b\mapsto(z\otimes1)\otimes b; these formulas are balanced and mutually inverse. They give exactly the twist identifications in the statement. The scalar functor is exact and additive by the same derived-change-of-rings assertion, hence preserves shifts and finite biproducts with their inclusions and projections. Write D_R=R_S(1)[2]\oplus R_S and identify T_S D_A=D_B by these maps.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; identity-topos coefficient specialization

proof.text: Put \Lambda=\mathbf Z/N and let c_\Lambda:\Lambda_P\to\mu_{N,P}[2] be the Kummer Chern morphism of the fixed line bundle \mathcal O_P(1). Write E_{\Lambda R} for derived scalar extension on P. The definition of the scalar-extended Kummer class in [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] says that the upstairs morphism whose q-adjunct is h_R is c_R=E_{\Lambda R}(c_\Lambda). Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to the identity-topos ring tower \Lambda_P\to A_P\to B_P. Its canonical composition isomorphism \alpha:T_P E_{\Lambda A}\simeq E_{\Lambda B} is natural on c_\Lambda, so \alpha_{\mu_N[2]}T_P(c_A)=c_B\alpha_{\Lambda_P}. The source component is the multiplication unit, and the target component is the balanced map of Step 1: the cited comparison is computed by ordinary module pullback composition on K-flat complexes. Therefore T_P(c_A)=c_B under the specified identifications. This is naturality of the image of one fixed Kummer morphism; it does not tensor the Kummer short exact sequence with a nonflat coefficient ring. The hypotheses of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] hold for R=A,B: S is of finite type over the Noetherian scheme \operatorname{Spec}k, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, so it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings); N=\ell^n is invertible on S because \ell\ne p=\operatorname{char}k; and A,B are finite commutative rings with NA=NB=0.

source.place: Charts: Kummer classes over A and B are images of the same class over Z/ell^n; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text:
Let \lambda_X:q_B^*T_SX\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Pq_A^*X be the canonical tensor/pullback comparison. It is the left square whose right mate is the specified \beta_q: this is precisely the proper counit-transpose normalization in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. For any v:q_A^*X\to E let \operatorname{adj}_R denote the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction bijection over R. Apply [lem-pur-adjunction-mate-transpose] to this square. It gives the equality of actual morphisms
$$\beta_q(E)T_S(\operatorname{adj}_A(v))=\operatorname{adj}_B(T_P(v)\lambda_X).$$
The orientation can also be checked directly: the B-transpose of the left side is T_P(\varepsilon_{A,E})\lambda_{Rq_{*,A}E}q_B^*T_S(\operatorname{adj}_A(v)); naturality of \lambda and the A-triangle identity turn this into T_P(v)\lambda_X. Thus the equality uses the named counit-transpose map rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism between the endpoints.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; transpose of the coefficient square, using the categorical mate-transpose identity

proof.text:
Write u_R:q_R^*(R_S(1)[2])\xrightarrow{\sim}L_R for pullback of the roots-of-unity twist. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] it is the canonical roots-induced identification. It satisfies T_P(u_A)\lambda_{A_S(1)[2]}=u_B under Step 1: both composites before shifting send (q^{-1}z\otimes a)\otimes b to the pulled-back root z\otimes\varphi(a)b. Equality of these sheaf maps gives equality of their degree-zero and shifted derived maps. The tensor and unit comparisons used here are the canonical ones of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The two components of s_R are \operatorname{adj}_R(u_R) and \operatorname{adj}_R(c_R), by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Apply Step 3 first to v=u_A and then to v=c_A; Step 2 identifies the scalar extension in the second application. Consequently
$$\beta_q(L_A)T_S(\operatorname{adj}_A(u_A))=\operatorname{adj}_B(u_B),\qquad \beta_q(L_A)T_S(h_A)=h_B.$$
Here q_B^*T_S A_S=B_P, so the latter equality has the asserted unit source, not a restriction-of-scalars source.

source.place: Charts: compare the twisted-unit and Kummer components of the two rank-one summands

proof.text:
Let \iota_{1,R},\iota_{2,R} be the two inclusions of D_R. Step 1 identifies T_S(\iota_{j,A}) with \iota_{j,B}. For j=1,2 Step 4 therefore gives
$$\beta_q(L_A)T_S(s_A)\iota_{j,B}=s_B\iota_{j,B}.$$
The universal property of the coproduct D_B says that maps out of it agreeing on both inclusions agree. Hence \beta_q(L_A)T_S(s_A)=s_B, the first required equation.

source.place: Charts: splitting into two free rank-one summands, compare both components

proof.text: Use the specified definition t_R=\operatorname{pr}_{2,R}s_R^{-1} of [def-amb-p1-trace]. Postcomposing the first equation with t_B gives t_B\beta_q(L_A)T_S(s_A)=\operatorname{pr}_{2,B}. Functoriality and Step 1 also give T_S(t_A)T_S(s_A)=T_S(\operatorname{pr}_{2,A})=\operatorname{pr}_{2,B}. Since s_A is invertible, T_S(s_A) is invertible with inverse T_S(s_A^{-1}); cancel it on the right. This proves t_B\beta_q(L_A)=T_S(t_A). All tensor computations were made on K-flat objects, and the other steps used functoriality, adjunction and coproduct identities. No flatness of B over A is used.

split_report.summary: Proved scalar compatibility by naturality of derived coefficient composition on the common Kummer Chern morphism, the proper counit-transpose identity on its two components, the coproduct universal property, and cancellation for the normalized trace. Reused existing nodes throughout; no new nodes and no statement change.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the Charts paragraph of det-sp-reduction-exceptional: Kummer classes come from Z/ell^n, compare the two summands of the projective-line splitting, then the trace projection. The six steps expand the retained Steps 5 and 6 named in the item source.

tool_uses.why: Canonical roots-induced ordinary-etale twist pullback, used to compare the first splitting component.
Ordinary-etale local freeness and flatness of finite twists for arbitrary finite coefficients.
Existing ordinary-etale normalized splitting and definition of its unit and Kummer components; coefficient compatibility is proved here.
General ringed-site bounded-flat K-flatness to compute extension of the two degree-zero lines; the unit does not replace this homological-algebra tool.
Generic categorical formula for a transpose under an already specified mate square; it supplies no geometric projective-line conclusion.
General ordinary ringed-site derived extension and its exactness, used for the specified ordinary-etale functor.
General ringed-topos composition and unit normalization, specialized to the identity-topos coefficient tower; it does not assert the projective-line compatibility being proved.
Only the stated proper counit-transpose normalization of beta is used; the site comparison and compactification assertions are not used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q69-43c3ababb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 6 steps in full, plus the statement of every cited node, the unit sk-lem-sp-reduction, the parent det-sp-reduction-exceptional (step 2) and the blueprint main-20261015 sk-lem-sp-reduction-exceptional.proof.md, Charts paragraph (lines 20-36). The split follows the Charts route: the Kummer class comes from Z/N, and the splitting has two free rank-one summands with trace = projection. No SGA source is cited. I found no duplicate. No node of sk-prop-geo-p1-adjunction states coefficient change of the splitting: det-sp-p1-trace and lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction cover base change only, and lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base covers only Z/l^r->Z/l^m reductions of gamma. lem-sp-p1-counit-scalar is the sibling counit lemma. Step 1: twist-line flatness, the K-flat closure and the termwise derived change of rings are correct; I checked that the balanced map and its inverse are mutually inverse on generators. Step 2: c_R=E_{Lambda R}(c_Lambda) is the defining construction in the p1-adjunction statement. The ringed-topos composition lemma, applied to the identity topos with Lambda->A->B, needs no flatness, and its unit equation gives the source component. Step 3: I checked the transpose formula myself; it follows from naturality of lambda and the A triangle identity, matching the B-adjoint-transpose definition of beta in lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility and det-sp-reduction-direct-image. Step 4: I checked T_P(u_A)lambda=u_B on generators; both splitting components are adj(u_R) and adj(c_R). Steps 5 and 6 (coproduct property, cancellation) are elementary. Edge cases: a non-flat map Z/l^2->F_l, the identity map, empty S and N=1 all work. The 8 declared tool uses are accepted. FIX: step 2 applied lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction without checking that S is Noetherian with N invertible. I added that check, citing the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian and using l != p, and added the node to uses and proof_deps.
